title: M9 Extension points: plugin protocol extracted from a signup-form plugin
description:
## Outcome
A simple deploy-time extension protocol, extracted from one real plugin (a signup form), lets a plugin contribute backend models/mutations, a newsroom panel, and a Markus directive with a self-contained web component on static pages.

## Design
/Users/home/Projects/markus-publication-architecture-v2.md section 7 (Extension points, later).

## Checklist
- [ ] SignupEntry model (not guest-readable)
- [ ] Guest submitSignup custom mutation: validation, honeypot, WAF rate rule
- [ ] Newsroom list + CSV export panel (editor/admin)
- [ ] :::signup directive via Markus Registry.register(DirectiveSpec) emitting <papyrus-signup> placeholder + versioned script; web component uploaded by project_all
- [ ] Extract the protocol (backend contribution through site-backend.ts like features switches; resolver waves; pinned versions; no compatibility shims) into docs

## Acceptance
- A page with :::signup on a test site renders statically; submitting the form creates a SignupEntry visible in the newsroom panel; 21st request per minute from one IP is blocked.

## Out of scope
A plugin registry, runtime hot-plugging, a second plugin.

## Dependencies
Blocked by M8 (public surface, WAF pattern) and M1 (projection Lambda).

## Risk
Abuse of guest writes; mitigated by WAF, validation, non-public storage.

## Estimate
6-10 agent-hours.
right_now_summary: Work is waiting on M8 and M1 before the signup plugin protocol can be built.
